science.title: ‘Vacuumtronics’ could help make better superconductors
science.snippet: Vacuum fluctuations can enhance superconductivity in a bulk material. This is the new finding from researchers in China and the US who have put forward the concept of “vacuumtronics”. This is a new way to tune superconductivity without chemically altering a material, applying pressure to it or driving it with intense light. In quantum electrodynamics, a vacuum is not empty but is host to fluctuating electromagnetic fields in which pairs of virtual particles are continuously being created and annihilated. Such vacuum fluctuations are thought to be responsible for phenomena like the Lamb shift , spontaneous emission and the Casimir effect . In recent years researchers have been looking into the possibility of exploiting these fluctuations to change the properties of bulk matter. science.snippet: arXiv:2610.22484v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The input space of single-spike neural networks decomposes into causal pieces, and the number of causal pieces has been shown to provide a lower bound on the approximation error for some spiking neural networks. While this decomposition is applicable to a wide range of spiking neuron models, the limits of how many causal pieces can be realised by spiking neural networks are still unknown. First, we establish a combinatorial bound given by the poly-Bernoulli numbers, which applies to a broad class of spiking neuron models. science.title: Large condensation in enriched $\infty$-categories
science.snippet: arXiv:2506.23632v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We demonstrate that many algebraic features of higher condensation theory are really features of higher algebra. We work in the context of monads on the unit of a monoidal 2- category. Assuming that 2-categorical unstraightening is monoidal, we show that the functor which takes such a monad to its Eilenberg-Moore object is lax monoidal. We use this to introduce an analog of condensation for codimension-i symmetries, without assuming dualizability. We give sufficient conditions for Morita equivalence of endomorphisms of condensates. We relate higher centralizers to iterated categories of modules. Along the way, we prove results pertaining to functoriality of Day convolution for enriched infinity-categories, which may be of independent interest.

science.title: All-multiplicity $\textrm{AdS}_4$ correlators in the self-dual sector
science.snippet: arXiv:2610.32957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It was recently shown that tree-level gluon correlators of any multiplicity in $\textrm{AdS}_4$ admit an expansion in terms of flat-space scattering amplitudes, where lower-point amplitudes in the expansion depend on merged external data. We derive here analogous formulae for correlators of scalar theories which encode the self-dual sectors of Yang-Mills theory and gravity in this background. In the latter case, the amplitudes are differential operators which can be obtained from the former using a simple double copy prescription in terms of kinematic numerators satisfying color-kinematics duality.

reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.38110v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are widely deployed in safety- and privacy-critical domains such as healthcare and finance, where models are trained on confidential data. In this paper we show that parameter evolutions of Brill-Lindquist-deSitter initial data mimic many of the features of that evolution.
